title: Visiting Assistant Professor of Economics
description:
Position Description

About the O’Malley School of Business:

The O’Malley School of Business prepares students for rewarding and
exceptional careers. The curriculum combines modern business theory
with immersive, real-world practice, providing the skills students
need to creatively solve the challenges of tomorrow. Since the
O’Malley School is one of only 5% of business schools worldwide
accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of
Business (AACSB), its students are sought after by many top
companies, across a broad spectrum of industries. The O'Malley
School of Business has many high-profile alumni connections and has
recently renovated classrooms and learning spaces.

The Department of Economics and Finance invites applications for a
full-time Visiting Assistant Professor of Economics for Academic
Year 2027-28, with the possibility of renewal for Academic Year
2028-29. The preferred field is international economics (trade,
international finance, or development); strong candidates in other
applied fields will be considered.

The successful candidate will teach a 4/4 load that includes
introductory and upper-level undergraduate courses and may include
graduate courses. Examples include Principles of Microeconomics,
Principles of Macroeconomics, Intermediate Microeconomics, and
International Economics.

Anticipated opening for Fall 2027, pending budget approval
(anticipated Spring 2027).

Job Responsibilities

In this role, you’ll have the opportunity to:

Teach a 4/4 load (four courses per semester) of introductory,
upper-level, and possibly graduate courses, such as Principles of
Microeconomics, Principles of Macroeconomics, Intermediate
Microeconomics, and International Economics.
Develop and maintain an inclusive, student-centered learning
environment that supports diverse learners, particularly first-year
students in the introductory sequence.
Hold regular office hours and provide academic advising and
mentorship that support student success, career preparation, and
graduate school pathways.
Maintain an active research program in economics leading to
peer-reviewed publications.
Contribute to departmental service and student engagement
activities.
Other duties as assigned.

Requirements

Ph.D. in Economics or a closely related field, with a research
focus in international economics preferred.
ABD candidates will be considered if they are on track to
complete their doctorate by or before the date of hire.
Demonstrated ability or strong potential for excellence in
undergraduate teaching, including Principles of Microeconomics and
Macroeconomics, and the ability to teach Intermediate
Microeconomics and International Economics.
Evidence of an active research agenda and potential for
publication in peer-reviewed journals.
Ability to teach and mentor a diverse student body.
Collaborative approach to academic service.

Supplemental Information

Please Submit:

Cover letter.
Curriculum vitae.
Teaching statement.
Evidence of teaching effectiveness, including course
evaluations and teaching observations.
Research statement.
Job market paper.
Contact information for three professional references.
Finalists will be asked to provide three letters of
recommendation.

Applications received by March 1, 2027 will receive full
consideration. Review of applications will begin in March 2027 and
continue until the position is filled. Questions may be directed to
Dr. Jimena González-Ramírez, Chair, Department of Economics and
Finance, at jimena.gonzalez@manhattan.edu.
